name: Cold spoons

lead: Cold spoons are spoons chilled in the freezer and held against the eye area to reduce puffiness.
Only a thin forum discussion exists and no studies have tested it.

paras: Cold is said to narrow blood vessels and reduce fluid in the tissue temporarily.
Ice directly on skin can cause cold burns; forum users also voice unverified nerve-damage worries.

lead: Cold spoons refers to pressing a spoon chilled in a freezer or fridge against the skin around the eyes to reduce puffiness or bloat. It is a home practice discussed in a few forum threads and has no published research behind it.

Looksmax.org users ask whether the method is legitimate, with one reply saying cold encourages blood flow and reduces swelling, and another thread participant recalling forum claims that ice can cause nerve damage.[1] A general reference describes cold compression as sometimes recommended for swelling, with evidence that is mixed, and notes that ice applied directly to skin can cause burns.[2]

paras: The practice borrows from cold compresses: the cold object is held briefly against the eye area. Cold is described as narrowing blood vessels and reducing fluid leaking into tissue, presented as a short-term effect.[3]

Reference material on cold therapy reports that ice applied directly to skin can cause cold burns and that serious injuries have followed excessive cooling time with powered devices.[2] The reference does not mention nerve injury; the nerve-damage claim in forum discussion is not substantiated by the sources reviewed.[1]
No studies found on cold spoons. Research on cold compression in sprains and post-surgical swelling is a different setting, and a review found insufficient evidence for acute ankle sprains.[2]

lore.intro: Cold spoons appear in a small number of threads about debloating.
